title: Dual size check (Content-Length + actual bytes) must stay for both endpoints
description: Every response body is checked twice: once against Content-Length (if present) for an early-exit optimization, and once against the actual bytes after read(). A contributor might suggest removing the post-read check as redundant. It is not: Content-Length is advisory and can be forged. A misbehaving server can lie in the header and deliver a larger body. Both checks are required. The early Content-Length check avoids buffering oversized bodies (optimization); the post-read check is the security guarantee. Remove either and the guarantee is weakened.
